 Home Alexander Zverev Rafael Jodar’s coach criticized after what he did during defeat to Alexander Zverev at the ATP Finals 
 Cameron Greenlees Sun 15 November 2026 15:34, UK Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images Follow us on Google Discover Alexander Zverev got off to a winning start in his ATP Finals campaign by beating Rafael Jodar in straight sets. 
 Zverev did not have his serve broken once in a fairly comfortable 6-4, 6-4 victory over the 20-year-old Spaniard, which puts him at the top of the John McEnroe group for now. The world number one still has to play Ben Shelton and Arthur Fils in the round-robin phase. 
 Photo by Mathias Schulz/Newhouse Media/MB Media/Getty Images Jamie Murray reacts to Alexander Zverev beating Rafael Jodar
 It was a superb start for Zverev, but a tough day at the office for Jodar, who is coached by his father, Rafael Jodar Sr. Analysing the debutant’s performance on Sky Sports , former British player Jamie Murray said: “I think it was a tough match for him.
 “The fact that Zverev served as well as he did, he’s not giving him any chance to get into points and rally and build pressure that way. There’s always a lot of pressure on his own serve. It was a tough first out for him. I think he acquitted himself pretty well, really. I think he’s probably more excited about other matches that he’s got to come.
 Which player do you think will win the 2026 ATP Finals?
 12 comments Comment Like or Comment Have your say Sign-in now for free “For me, it was just interesting to watch the dad. I sat a few seats down from him. Their relationship, how they go about things on the court, is very unique. I’m watching, and he’s looking for the dad a lot after a lot of points, especially ones that he loses. But the dad’s just looking down.
 “I kind of felt a bit bad for him in a way because he’s literally out there all by himself in this massive event, big stadium, first night there. I felt like he needed a bit more support. I think he just got bullied in a way, right? When Sasha was serving, games were going by so quick.
 “There was no chance for him to really get rhythm, find pressure, build pressure into the Zverev service games. It’s a meteoric rise that he’s got on these last 18 months, or whenever he decided to quit college and turn pro. For him to step out here and for us to expect that he would have all the answers for Sascha Zverev, who’s had the year of his life and is world number one, that’s a big ask, I think.”
 Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images Jamie Murray praises Alexander Zverev’s ‘godlike’ serve
 Zverev fired 10 aces past Jodar, while tallying a first-serve percentage of 84%. “I think it was an impressive performance,” said Murray. “I don’t know if Sascha is walking off the court thinking, I played amazing there.
 More Tennis News “I think he serves godlike, really. It was very impressive to sit courtside to see that up close and personal. I think he probably wasn’t feeling massively comfortable with his groundstrokes. But at the most important points, he kind of stepped up.
 “He was happy to take the ball on, play on his terms, and he got his rewards for that. Just the fact that he can serve plus 220 and serve over 70-80% across the course of a match. When he served for the set at 5-4, he’d only missed one serve. He served 17 out of 18 serves. Granted, this is his first match of the tournament as well.
 “First match as world number one. There are obviously nerves going into that. For him not to miss one serve, that’s scary. It’s so rare you would see a player serve over 85-90% in a set. But for him, it’s not that uncommon.”
 Zverev has the second-highest serve rating on the ATP Tour with 303.5, trailing only Jannik Sinner (305.6).
